summary: Annette L. Heitmann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and completed her doctorate at the University of Vienna by 2002, studying under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Berlin (around 1989–1994) and her habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (2008), where she serves on the Indology faculty.

Anthony C. Yu worked in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD 1969), where he served on the faculty from around 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from 2001 to 2007 and was appointed Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin–Madison around 2014.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a Sinologist and historian. He studied under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak at Leiden University in 1928, later becoming a lecturer in Chinese there in 1946 and professor from 1956 to 1975.

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough and William Stede (around 1949–1954), taught Sanskrit at Edinburgh (1955–1963), and chaired East Asian Studies at Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson in 1995; his academic posts include the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
Anthony W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1984 and later held a post at the University of Calgary.
Antoine Lutz specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist, Iranologist, and Indologist who studied at the Sorbonne and EPHE under Ferdinand de Saussure, Sylvain Lévi, and James Darmesteter. He held professorships at INALCO (1902–1906) and the Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist, Iranologist, and historian. He held chairs at INALCO from 1795 and at the Collège de France from 1806 to 1838, and served as rector of the University of Paris in 1815.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was a French scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later holding the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France from 1815 until 1832.

Anton Boller was an Austrian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a lecturer and professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Vienna from 1845 until 1855 and beyond.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Berlin around 1828–1831 and later taught Oriental and modern Occidental languages there from 1849 to 1852.

Anton Schiefner was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg and Berlin, held positions at the Imperial Academy of Sciences starting in 1852, and taught classics at Saint Petersburg Roman Catholic Theological Academy.
Anton Westermann was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied and completed his habilitation at the University of Leipzig (1825–1830), where he served as co-director from 1830 to 1865.

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He held research positions at the Italian School of East Asian Studies around 2004 and at SOAS University of London between 2005 and 2010.

Antonino Forte was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (around 1982–1999) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (around 1989–2006).
Antonio T. de Nicolás was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD from Fordham University and served as a professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University beginning around 1968.

Antonio Terrone works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University in 2010 under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and later became a scholar in residence at BDRC.
